bull_bear.body:
- **Net cash** position (~₹116 cr net cash; gross debt ~₹230 cr; total cash ₹3,931 mn). Pre-tax operating cash flow ₹2,866 mn; **cash conversion 98%**.
- **No equity raise** planned for the 5,000-bed program — funded by cash + internal accruals + measured debt.
- Working-capital discipline: debtor days 124→112, targeting 90–95 in FY27. Year-end FDs parked centrally for best returns (drove "other financial assets" jump on balance sheet).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **New-unit gestation drag:** ~₹30 cr combined EBITDA loss (Model Town + Faridabad Sec-20) until FY27-H2 breakeven; execution risk on ramp.
- **Interest cost creep** from Agra debt; more debt likely as expansion continues.
- **Oncology drug price control / supply:** Government price caps hit ~20–30% of pricing within the ~10% oncology revenue pie; marginal but real impact; substitutes not easily available.
- **International-patient disruption:** Q1 FY27 dip from West Asia crisis / Bangladesh & Afghanistan closures (industry-wide); mgmt expects recovery + Africa offset.
- **Government payer concentration (~35%)** with CGHS-linked (lower) rates; Ayushman dilutive.
- **Income-tax matter:** Near final resolution (expected by end-Q2 FY27); mgmt sees no major liability; no assets/FDs frozen.
- **Competitive NCR market** with larger players.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident and expansion-forward. Repeatedly guided to **surpassing** FY26's growth in FY27 on both topline and EBITDA. Emphasized disciplined, geography-led, capex-per-bed-driven acquisition criteria and a "doctor-friendly, non-P&L-target" culture that attracts clinical talent. Proactive on governance (BDO/MSKA statutory auditor — first results under BDO; Deloitte internal auditor; new Independent Director Ramesh Krishan). Candid on new-unit losses and tax matter.
bull_bear.title: Management tone

bull_bear.body:
- Agra was acquired **already profitable** (18% EBITDA margin, ~₹7 cr/mo run-rate) — it is NOT a drag, contrary to the typical acquisition-dilution assumption; contributes ~18% (mentioned by CFO). First Da Vinci robot in the region.
- The reported-vs-adjusted margin gap (~7pp in Q4) is a quantifiable, time-bound "self-healing" lever — pure new-unit ramp losses, not structural.
- CGHS rate-hike benefit is staged (different schemes implemented at different times); full ~5% revenue effect only from FY27.
- Brownfield expansions deliberately deferred (not stalled) — capacity timed to occupancy need; cheap at ~₹75 lakh/bed (land + shared infra already sunk).
- Noida Extension oncology mix jumped ~20%→~30% via surgical oncology + BMT — a high-margin mix shift driving the +23% ARPOB.
- "Boutique hospital" positioning as differentiation vs large impersonal corporate hospitals in NCR.

- "First Interim Dividend 5% of Face Value", framed as "Balancing shareholder returns with growth investments"; also listed as "First Interim Dividend Announced in Aug-26".

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographical concentration of operations in Delhi NCR — The MD&A Risk Management section states that despite its established presence in the Delhi NCR, the Company remains conscious of the geographical concentration of its operations - the network's earnings depend heavily on a single regional catchment and on NCR-specific competitive, pricing and regulatory dynamics.
- Intense competition in the healthcare landscape — Management states the Company operates in a highly competitive healthcare landscape with a strong focus on advanced medical technology and quality patient care, requiring continuous investment simply to retain clinical positioning and patient share.
- Dependence on skilled medical professionals and talent retention — The Company prioritises talent retention through continuous training and a supportive workplace culture, recognising the importance of skilled medical professionals in sustaining long-term growth - clinician attrition would directly impair case mix and service delivery.
- Evolving regulatory requirements — Management identifies evolving regulatory requirements as a challenge it addresses through robust risk management and operational discipline; the cautionary statement additionally names modifications to tax laws and government regulations as important variables that might affect performance.
- Economic uncertainties and inflationary pressures — The Risk Management section names economic uncertainties and inflationary pressures among the challenges the Company must address; the cautionary statement adds Indian economic conditions as a variable that could cause results to differ greatly from expectations.
- Execution and integration risk from an expansion-led growth model — The Company added multiple hospitals through acquisition (Sector 20 Faridabad, Model Town New Delhi, Agra, and the under-construction Gurugram facility) and states its focus remains on disciplined capital allocation and operational integration - the growth model depends on ramping newly added facilities to acceptable utilisation.
- Reliance on internal controls scaled to a rapidly growing operation — The internal control system is described as designed to correspond to the size and complexity of the operations and the incremental changes made, supplemented by an internal audit programme reporting to the Audit and Risk Management Committee - the control framework must keep pace with a network expanding by acquisition.

outlook.body: Yatharth pursues a cluster-based expansion model, deepening leadership in established clusters (Noida, Faridabad), selectively entering underserved high-growth markets, and replicating its proven clinical and operating model across new facilities. During FY 2025-26 the network expanded to nine hospitals, comprising seven facilities across Delhi-NCR, one in Agra (Uttar Pradesh) and one in Jhansi-Orchha (Madhya Pradesh), taking the network to more than 2,800 beds. Facilities added or acquired in recent years include Greater Faridabad / Sector 88 (2024), Sector 20 Faridabad (2025), Model Town New Delhi (2025) and Agra (2026); the Company also acquired a 100% controlling stake in Shanti Ved Institute of Medical Sciences Private Limited on January 29, 2026, and made an investment in connection with the acquisition of a hospital in Agra. To seed its next cluster, the Company acquired an under-construction, ultra-modern super-speciality hospital in Sector 40, Gurugram - a proposed 250-bed facility with a proposed outlay of Rs 200 Crore including medical equipment, expected to commence operations in April 2027 (Q1 FY28). Beyond that, the Company has announced brownfield capacity additions of 200 beds at Greater Noida and 250 beds at Noida Extension over the next 24 months, and has set out a target of 5,000 beds over the next three years. Clinical capability build-out during the year included installation of advanced oncology equipment and PET-CT technology, adoption of robotic-assisted knee replacement surgery and deployment of the Da Vinci Robotic Surgical System. Internationally, the Company is establishing Medical Value Travel information centres in Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Mauritius, Tanzania and Kenya, and has established representative offices in Tashkent and Baghdad; it has also been empanelled as the dedicated healthcare service provider for Noida International Airport, Jewar.

deepdive.thesis: Yatharth is a North-India (NCR + UP) multi-specialty hospital roll-up executing a disciplined **cluster-based** expansion (become the largest player across micro-markets within a city), funded largely by internal accruals with a **net cash** balance sheet. FY26 was "transformative": revenue +36% YoY, three new hospitals added (~1,000 beds), Agra acquired, and Gurugram cluster seeded. During FY 2025-26 the network expanded to nine hospitals, comprising seven facilities across Delhi-NCR, one in Agra (Uttar Pradesh) and one in Jhansi-Orchha (Madhya Pradesh), taking the network to more than 2,800 beds. Facilities added or acquired in recent years include Greater Faridabad / Sector 88 (2024), Sector 20 Faridabad (2025), Model Town New Delhi (2025) and Agra (2026); the Company also acquired a 100% controlling stake in Shanti Ved Institute of Medical Sciences Private Limited on January 29, 2026, and made an investment in connection with the acquisition of a hospital in Agra. To seed its next cluster, the Company acquired an under-construction, ultra-modern super-speciality hospital in Sector 40, Gurugram - a proposed 250-bed facility with a proposed outlay of Rs 200 Crore including medical equipment, expected to commence operations in April 2027 (Q1 FY28). Beyond that, the Company has announced brownfield capacity additions of 200 beds at Greater Noida and 250 beds at Noida Extension over the next 24 months, and has set out a target of 5,000 beds over the next three years. Clinical capability build-out during the year included installation of advanced oncology equipment and PET-CT technology, adoption of robotic-assisted knee replacement surgery and deployment of the Da Vinci Robotic Surgical System. Internationally, the Company is establishing Medical Value Travel information centres in Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Mauritius, Tanzania and Kenya, and has established representative offices in Tashkent and Baghdad; it has also been empanelled as the dedicated healthcare service provider for Noida International Airport, Jewar.

thesis: Yatharth is a North-India (NCR + UP) multi-specialty hospital roll-up executing a disciplined **cluster-based** expansion (become the largest player across micro-markets within a city), funded largely by internal accruals with a **net cash** balance sheet. FY26 was "transformative": revenue +36% YoY, three new hospitals added (~1,000 beds), Agra acquired, and Gurugram cluster seeded. The investable angle is the **gap between reported and adjusted margins** — new-unit ramp drag suppresses headline EBITDA (23.4% Q4 reported vs 30.4% adjusted), so as Model Town and Faridabad Sec-20 hit breakeven in FY27-H2 and newer hospitals (higher ARPOB ~₹40k) scale, group ARPOB and margin should re-rate upward. Mgmt guides to **surpassing** FY26's 36% revenue growth in FY27 and a path to **5,000 beds in ≤3 years** (3,200 already reached).

FY26 was "transformative": revenue +36% YoY, three new hospitals added (~1,000 beds), Agra acquired, and Gurugram cluster seeded. The investable angle is the **gap between reported and adjusted margins** — new-unit ramp drag suppresses headline EBITDA (23.4% Q4 reported vs 30.4% adjusted), so as Model Town and Faridabad Sec-20 hit breakeven in FY27-H2 and newer hospitals (higher ARPOB ~₹40k) scale, group ARPOB and margin should re-rate upward. Mgmt guides to **surpassing** FY26's 36% revenue growth in FY27 and a path to **5,000 beds in ≤3 years** (3,200 already reached).

**CALL OUT — new-unit gestation drag:** Model Town (−₹21 cr EBITDA) and Faridabad Sec-20 (−₹9 cr EBITDA) together create ~2% EBITDA drag on the consolidated pie. This is the entire gap between 23.4% reported and 30.4% adjusted Q4 margin. Both guided to EBITDA breakeven in **FY27-H2**.
guidance (critical):
- **Beds:** Target **5,000 beds in ≤3 years** (mgmt thinks possibly earlier); 3,200 already reached. Mix of incremental beds: **~70% acquisitions, ~30% greenfield**. Brownfield at Greater Noida & Noida Extension on track (construction started at GN).
- **Occupancy / ARPOB:** Large headroom in new units (32%/52%/52%). ARPOB growth guided to **~10% p.a.** going forward (vs +7% FY26); newer hospitals running ~₹40k ARPOB vs group ₹33k → mix-led uplift. Gurugram expected ARPOB **>₹50,000**.
- **Margin:** FY full-year EBITDA margin guidance **24–25%** (consistent track record); mgmt expects FY27 EBITDA margin to be **better** than FY26 despite new-unit additions.
- **Revenue:** FY27 revenue growth to **surpass** FY26's +36% YoY.
- **Capex:** No equity raise planned for the 5,000-bed plan — funded by cash + internal accruals + some debt. Gurugram: ~₹100 cr upfront + ~₹100 cr fit-out/medical infra.
- **Debtor days:** FY25 124 → FY26 112 → **FY27 target 90–95 days**.
- **Payer mix:** Government payer ~35% currently (down 2–3% YoY) → target **~25% in ~2 years**; new hospitals targeting <10–12% government.
- **Breakeven timelines:** Faridabad Sec-20 ~10–11 mo; Model Town ~14–15 mo; both EBITDA breakeven by FY27-H2. Gurugram ~13–15 mo from operational (Apr-2027).
pipeline (beds under development / m&a):
- **Gurugram Sector 40** — ultra-modern under-construction super-speciality; ₹100 cr upfront + ~₹100 cr fit-out; operational **April 2027**; ARPOB >₹50k; tertiary/quaternary, self-pay + insurance + international mix; near IGI Airport. Seeds the new Gurugram cluster.
- **Brownfield: Greater Noida** — structural drawings finalized, basic construction started; capex ~₹75 lakh/bed (ex-land, since land + shared infra already owned).
- **Brownfield: Noida Extension** — similar phase; legal formalities complete; timed to occupancy ramp need.
- **5,000-bed roadmap** — 70% acquisitions / 30% greenfield, focused on NCR + bigger North-India cities (UP, Haryana, Punjab metros). UP cluster (Agra/Jhansi) seen as large untapped runway.
segment — mature vs new units:
- **Mature units (Noida cluster + Jhansi + old Faridabad):** Driving ARPOB through OPD→IPD conversion, maturing super-specialities (new treatment lines), and rising **international patients** (esp. Greater Noida & Noida Extension). Noida Extension oncology share ~30% (from ~20%), driven by surgical oncology + bone-marrow transplants + new oncology team.
- **New units (Model Town, Faridabad Sec-20, Agra):** Strong ramp ahead of internal expectations; superior initial ARPOB (~₹38–40k) and favorable cash/TPA payer mix. Together the 2 newest units = ~11% of Q4 revenue. Agra (acquired profitable) is a feeder hub for oncology/high-value specialities; installed Agra's first Da Vinci robot (50 robotic surgeries done).
growth / optionality:
- **Medical value travel:** Exclusive hospital partner for now-operational **Noida International Airport (Jewar)** — international flights soon; Noida-zone medical tourism ecosystem on rising trend. Outreach in Middle East, CIS; pivoting strongly to **African market** (senior resources deployed, 2–3 medical centers starting).
- **Cluster roll-up:** Largest-player density in micro-markets (Noida 3 hospitals, Faridabad 2, Gurugram seeded). Brand-building helps attract star clinicians.
- **CGHS rate revision (Dec-2025):** +5% overall revenue uplift, >3% flowing to EBITDA; full effect in FY27.
- **Speciality mix upgrade:** Spreading super-speciality cases (oncology, neuro, GI/POEM, cardiac) across all units; radiation oncology to start at Faridabad Sec-20 and Model Town.
margins & cost:
- Reported EBITDA margin 23.4% (Q4) / 24.2% (FY) suppressed by new-unit losses; **adjusted 30.4% / 28.5%**. FY guidance 24–25%; FY27 expected better.
- CGHS rate hike adds ~5% revenue / >3% EBITDA.
- Payer-mix shift toward cash / private insurance / international (higher realization) and away from government (35%→25% target) supports margin.
- Margin profile varies by procedure even within government schemes (oncology, cardiac higher-margin); Ayushman lower margin than CGHS/ECHS/ESI.
capex:
- **Gurugram:** ₹100 cr upfront + ~₹100 cr fit-out/medical infra.
- **Brownfield (Greater Noida + Noida Extension):** ~₹75 lakh/bed (ex-land; shared towers/equipment already in place); no cost escalation expected.
- Agra: funded via debt (the source of the QoQ interest-cost rise).
capital allocation:
- **Net cash** position (~₹116 cr net cash; gross debt ~₹230 cr; total cash ₹3,931 mn). Pre-tax operating cash flow ₹2,866 mn; **cash conversion 98%**.
- **No equity raise** planned for the 5,000-bed program — funded by cash + internal accruals + measured debt.
- Working-capital discipline: debtor days 124→112, targeting 90–95 in FY27. Year-end FDs parked centrally for best returns (drove "other financial assets" jump on balance sheet).
risks:
- **New-unit gestation drag:** ~₹30 cr combined EBITDA loss (Model Town + Faridabad Sec-20) until FY27-H2 breakeven; execution risk on ramp.
- **Interest cost creep** from Agra debt; more debt likely as expansion continues.
- **Oncology drug price control / supply:** Government price caps hit ~20–30% of pricing within the ~10% oncology revenue pie; marginal but real impact; substitutes not easily available.
- **International-patient disruption:** Q1 FY27 dip from West Asia crisis / Bangladesh & Afghanistan closures (industry-wide); mgmt expects recovery + Africa offset.
- **Government payer concentration (~35%)** with CGHS-linked (lower) rates; Ayushman dilutive.
- **Income-tax matter:** Near final resolution (expected by end-Q2 FY27); mgmt sees no major liability; no assets/FDs frozen.
- **Competitive NCR market** with larger players.
management tone: Confident and expansion-forward. Repeatedly guided to **surpassing** FY26's growth in FY27 on both topline and EBITDA. Emphasized disciplined, geography-led, capex-per-bed-driven acquisition criteria and a "doctor-friendly, non-P&L-target" culture that attracts clinical talent. Proactive on governance (BDO/MSKA statutory auditor — first results under BDO; Deloitte internal auditor; new Independent Director Ramesh Krishan). Candid on new-unit losses and tax matter.
non-obvious points:
- Agra was acquired **already profitable** (18% EBITDA margin, ~₹7 cr/mo run-rate) — it is NOT a drag, contrary to the typical acquisition-dilution assumption; contributes ~18% (mentioned by CFO). First Da Vinci robot in the region.
- The reported-vs-adjusted margin gap (~7pp in Q4) is a quantifiable, time-bound "self-healing" lever — pure new-unit ramp losses, not structural.
- CGHS rate-hike benefit is staged (different schemes implemented at different times); full ~5% revenue effect only from FY27.
- Brownfield expansions deliberately deferred (not stalled) — capacity timed to occupancy need; cheap at ~₹75 lakh/bed (land + shared infra already sunk).
- Noida Extension oncology mix jumped ~20%→~30% via surgical oncology + BMT — a high-margin mix shift driving the +23% ARPOB.
- "Boutique hospital" positioning as differentiation vs large impersonal corporate hospitals in NCR.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- Oncology drug price control → patients route via CGHS/ECHS dispensaries; hospital pivots to radiation/surgical oncology + BMT (less affected sub-streams). ⭐ Net-net Yatharth manages around it; CGHS rate hike offsets.
- International-patient disruption (West Asia/Bangladesh/Afghanistan) → ✅ pivot to **African market** as offset.

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.
